title: Why France Toppled Its King
question: How did a money crisis turn into the end of France's monarchy?
hook: A kingdom that could not collect its own taxes ended up executing its king.
idea: An unfair tax system and a blocked government pushed France from a financial crisis into a revolution that replaced the monarchy with a republic.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: By 1788 half of state revenue went on servicing the monarchy's debt.
The nobility and Church had many exemptions, so the tax burden fell mainly on the lower classes.
The king could easily fix this by decree, since the parlements always accepted new laws.
The deadlock led to the calling of the Estates General of 1789.
beats.explain: Parlements could block new tax laws, and imposing laws by decree risked open conflict with them and the nobility.

beats.prompt: The finance minister proposes a universal land tax. A hand-picked Assembly of Notables dominated by the nobility votes on it. What happens?

choices.label: They approve it to help the king
choices.feedback: The nobility benefited from exemptions, so a tax on everyone threatened them.

choices.label: They hand the decision to the Third Estate
choices.feedback: The notables did not pass it on to commoners; they said an Estates-General had to decide.

beats.explain: The new taxes were rejected first by the nobility-dominated Assembly of Notables, then by the parlements.

beats.prompt: Match each person or group to what they did
pairs: Reconstituted itself as a National Assembly
Announced that an Estates-General would meet
Led the Jacobin-dominated Committee of Public Safety
beats.explain: Each acted at a turning point: forming the Assembly, proposing reform, calling the Estates-General, and leading the Committee.
The Estates General met in 1789, Louis XVI was executed in 1793, the Terror ended in 1794, and the coup came in 1799.
